title: Pipeline token surge bisect notes
content:
Context:
- Intermittent customer-reported slow streaming responses (SSE) from hosted endpoints during token surges (bursty user input). See ENG-2491 for initial report.
- Symptoms: first 1-3 chunks arrive promptly, then long pauses (200ms -> 1s -> 5s), then either a burst of many small chunks or abrupt stream termination with HTTP 200 but incomplete final message.
- Problem appears more visible on smaller models and shorter sequences but reproducible against larger ones too. Suspect interaction between prefetch/batching and KV-cache eviction/backpressure.

Quick reproduction attempts (local):
1) Simple curl SSE test (raw):
   export REDWOOD_API_KEY=redwood-FAKEKEY
   curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
     -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"rw-medium-1","prompt":"repeat x10000 \"token\"","stream":true}' \
     https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate/stream 
   -> Observed: consistent initial chunks then long gap, then flood of micro-chunks (0-5 bytes) that client coalesces slowly.

2) Node EventSource-ish repro (fetch with ReadableStream):
   node tests/stream-probe.js --concurrency 8 --burst 50
   -> When concurrency > 6, the tail latency escalates non-linearly. Suspect queueing in per-worker request loop.

3) Python asyncio client (aiohttp) to reproduce backpressure window:
   python tests/aio-stream-probe.py --burst 200 --delay 0.01
   -> Reproduced stalls at ~burst 120. Logs show server send() times cluster around same timestamps (bunching).

Server-side observations and commands run on a repro instance (dedicated dev pool):
- tail -f /var/log/redwood/serving-runtime.log | grep "stream-send"
  -> spikes in send latency recorded: send_latency_ms goes from 2ms to 1500ms in same connection.
- curl against /metrics endpoint: noticed backlog_queue_size metric increases under burst.
- tc qdisc added to dev host to simulate limited egress bandwidth: tc qdisc add dev eth0 root tbf rate 50mbit burst 10kb latency 50ms
  -> made problem worse (expected), but confirms sensitivity to network pacing.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Prefetch/pipelining to GPU + continuous batching causes uneven kernel occupancy: initial prefix requests serviced quickly, then a long GC/eviction on per-connection KV cache causes blocking while cache is compacted. Evidence: KV cache eviction logs correlate with first big gap.
2) Flow-control inside HTTP layer (chunk framing) interacts poorly with our streaming output buffer: when backend is ready it writes many tiny chunks; tcmalloc fragmentation + writev results in many syscalls and scheduling delays.
3) Backpressure semantics are not propagated end-to-end: when worker stalls on GPU, connection-level write buffers continue to accept data until OS buffer fills, then user-level network library yields but our runtime doesn't throttle upstream batching fast enough.
4) Edge case in SSE framing code that injects keepalive whitespace causing client libs to treat as heartbeat and not read subsequent chunk immediately (less likely).

Error snippets captured:
- serving-runtime.log:
  [2025-10-21T13:42:12.123Z] INFO conn=0x7f8b stream-send chunk_id=14 send_latency_ms=3
  [2025-10-21T13:42:12.427Z] INFO conn=0x7f8b stream-send chunk_id=15 send_latency_ms=1543 (KV-evict=true)
  [2025-10-21T13:42:13.980Z] WARN conn=0x7f8b writev-failed err=EAGAIN queued=32768

- client stdout (curl):
  data: {"token":"token","index":0}
  data: {"token":"token","index":1}
  [5s pause]
  data: {"token":"token","index":2}
  data: {"token":"token","index":3}
  [socket closed by server]

- pcap/tcpdump trace (timestamps):
  13:42:12.12 -> chunk 14 (200 bytes)
  13:42:12.43 -> chunk 15 (1 byte)
  13:42:13.98 -> socket FIN

Bisect notes (what I changed and effects):
- Disable KV-cache compaction (flag --kv-compact-interval=0): stalls gone in short runs but memory grows unbounded. Adds weight to hypothesis 1.
- Force per-connection write coalescing (writev aggregation up to 64kb): reduced syscall count but stalls still visible at high burst. Suggests syscall overhead is not the only issue.
- Turn off prefetching (kernel-level prefetch disable flag): latency profile is smoother but throughput drops 12%. Prefetch seems to cause the sharp stalls.
- Replaced tcmalloc with jemalloc on a dev instance: no meaningful change.

Reproduction recipe for next-person-to-debug
1) Spin up dev_dedicated_pool small instance (instructions in infra runbook).
2) Start runtime with flags:
   --log-level=debug --kv-compact-interval=30 --prefetch-windows=4 --stream-coalesce-size=64k
3) Run quick probe: node tests/stream-probe.js --burst 150 --concurrency 8 --out ./probe-output.json
4) Collect: /var/log/redwood/serving-runtime.log, /proc/<pid>/fdinfo/*, netstat -tanp, and pcap with filter host <client-ip> and port <port>.

Useful one-liners I ran:
- Show fd buffer sizes: for fd in $(ls /proc/$(pidof serving-runtime)/fd); do cat /proc/$(pidof serving-runtime)/fdinfo/$fd | grep -E "pos|flags|size" || true; done
- Attach perf to a stuck thread (useful when stalls > 500ms): sudo perf record -g -p $(pgrep serving-runtime) -F 99 -- sleep 5
- Quick tcpdump save (rotating): sudo timeout 30 tcpdump -i any host <client-ip> and port 443 -w /tmp/stream-probe.pcap

Open questions / next steps:
- Is KV-compact happening synchronously on request path? Need confirm in codepath (cache_manager::compact() call sites). If it is synchronous, change to background compaction or incremental compaction.
- If prefetch windows cause kernel contention, try adaptive prefetch (decrease windows when backlog_queue_size > threshold).
- Validate user-level flow-control: when worker sees EAGAIN on write, does it reduce batch_size or mark connection as backpressured? Add metrics for "connection_backpressured" and per-conn queued_bytes.
- Reproduce with HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 clients — is the behavior protocol-specific? I only tested HTTP/1.1 so far.

Notes-to-self for instrumentation patches:
- Add per-chunk trace_id and log traces through scheduling -> GPU queue -> write() so we can correlate kernel start/finish with send times.
- Emit metric: stream_tail_latency_p90 and per-conn queued_bytes.

Rough timeline (for incident writeup):
- 2025-10-18: first customer ticket (low severity)
- 2025-10-21: internal repro and initial bisect (disabled KV-compact reduced stalls)
- 2025-10-28: added write coalescing experiment (partial improvement)
- 2025-11-02: current snapshot, need background compaction and adaptive prefetch experiments in staging

Assorted crumbs / random observations:
- On macOS local, not reproducible reliably (likely due to different TCP stack and sandboxed GPU behavior).
- Some client libraries batch reads and only expose message on newline, so micro-chunks can be hidden and look like a pause. When possible, test with raw curl -N.
- Customer saw issue across regions; makes me think it's systemic rather than single node.

Action items (TODO):
- [ ] Add conn-level queued_bytes metric (low effort) -- assign Liam
- [ ] Make KV compaction async (design doc) -- assign Samira (me)
- [ ] Implement adaptive prefetch gating by backlog metric (POC) -- assign Priya
- [ ] Re-run large-burst repro with HTTP/2 client and include pcap -- assign QA

If you pick this up: start by running the node probe with --concurrency 4 and increase slowly; watch backlog_queue_size metric and serving-runtime logs (search for KV-evict).
